content:
alex: Heads up — seeing intermittent NCCL hangs on multi-GPU training across two racks in eu-west-1. Jobs spin waiting on allreduce, then recover after ~30s. Pattern looks networky, not CUDA OOM.

maria: Any packet loss or errors in dmesg/ibv?

alex: I pulled logs: some QP retries and a bunch of RoCE v2 PMTU errors. Kernel shows `TCP: Possible SYN flooding` noise too but that might be unrelated. Example from one host: 
```
rdma: ib_core: QP 0x3f3c going to error state, retry exceeded
mlx5_core 0000:84:00.0: mlx5e: RoCE v2 pkey mismatch on vlan?
NET: eth0: rx errors 120 tx errors 0 dropped 58 overruns 0
```

sam: Do you have `ethtool -S` and `ibv_devinfo` outputs? Could be offloaded VXLAN/encap path dropping large frames if MTU negotiation fails.

alex: Yep attached snippets (trimmed):
```
# ethtool -k eth0
rx-checksumming: on
lro: on
rxvlan: on
rx-nfc: off
# ibv_devinfo -v
device: mlx5_0
transport: RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE)
port 1: state: ACTIVE
port 1: gid table length: 128
```
No obvious pkey mismatch though.

jen: Could be asymmetric routing between ToR switches + ECMP rebalancing — that breaks PMTU for RoCEv2 because UDP encapsulation path changes. We saw similar last month but that was on a single AZ.

maria: Are you seeing this only when GPUs in different racks are used?

alex: Yes — intra-rack runs are fine. Cross-rack jobs show the spike. Also noticed when we push a firmware update to a set of ToRs, the pattern correlates.

dmitri: Are ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages making it back? Our network security sometimes blocks ICMP which breaks PMTU discovery. Check `tcpdump -n -i eth0 icmp or udp` while reproducing.

alex: Good call. I ran tcpdump and saw a few ICMP frag-needed from intermediate switch to host but the host never seemed to send them back to sender. Suspect device offloads swallowing ICMP. Example: `ICMP frag_needed, mtu 8900` then nothing on the other side.

sam: If NIC offloads drop those ICMPs, RoCEv2's large UDP packets get blackholed. Try disabling LRO/GRO and verify `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc` (should be 0). Also confirm `ip link show` MTU consistent along path.

alex: Did a quick experiment: disabled GRO/LRO on a host and re-ran job — NCCL hang didn't appear for that run. Re-enabled afterwards and the hang came back.

jen: That strongly indicates PMTU/encap issues. We should also check VXLAN/overlay settings on the ToRs — do they do UDP encapsulation for east-west? If so, outer MTU needs to be bigger.

oncall: Opening an infra incident to track cross-rack RoCE instability. I'll add packet captures, device offload state, and a list of affected hosts. Incident ID INF-2025-072.

ci-bot: Incident INF-2025-072 created by oncall. Severity: P2. Link: https://redwood.ops/incidents/INF-2025-072

maria: For short-term mitigation, we can enforce a smaller MTU on hosts (e.g., 8500) or force TCP/UDP PMTU probing via `ip route`->`mtu` settings. But that costs effective payload per packet.

dmitri: Another mitigation is to use RoCEv1 (if supported) or enable kernel-level PMTU blackhole recovery — not ideal. Longer term, we need consistent MTU across ToR->spine paths and not block ICMP.

sam: Also double-check switch firmware release notes — some versions had a bug dropping ICMP when UDP > 9k with VXLAN. Might explain the firmware correlation.

alex: Action items I/O: 1) Oncall/inciden't will collect pcap + `ethtool -k` + `ibv_devinfo` from affected hosts (doing now). 2) infra to verify ToR config and any recent fw pushes. 3) infra/sre to run a controlled job with GRO/LRO off and MTU 8500 to confirm mitigation.

jen: I'll schedule a maintenance window to test firmware rollback on a small ToR pair tomorrow 0200 UTC if infra signs off.

maria: Also we'll add an automated health-check that runs small NCCL allreduce across racks to flag this earlier (cheap smoke test).

alex: Thanks — will attach pcaps and logs to the incident ticket once uploaded. :thumbsup:

oncall: Affected job IDs and hosts attached to INF-2025-072. Will update when we have root-cause or next steps.

sam: FYI, if anyone needs to reproduce: run this short stress script that allocates 4 GPUs across two hosts and loops allreduce: 
```bash
# run on leader
mpirun -n 2 -H hostA,hostB python -c "import torch,torch.distributed as dist; dist.init_process_group('nccl'); ..."
```
keep tcpdump running on both hosts when you trigger.

alex: Uploaded logs + pcaps to the incident. Leaving traces here if anyone wants quick context.

jen: Thanks — we'll try the maintenance tomorrow and circle back in this thread. :spiral_calendar_pad:
